subject.title: improve: index transcript mirror persistence checks

question: Should OpenClaw publish `withSessionTranscriptIndexedWriteLock` and its three mirror-oriented persistence reads as a supported Plugin SDK contract, or keep the optimization behind a narrower internal/owner runtime seam?
rationale: The code can preserve the current callers either way, but only maintainers can choose the permanent external Plugin SDK boundary and its compatibility commitment.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow SDK contract
options.body: Approve the indexed lock as a reusable plugin API, then require current-head real behavior proof and focused compatibility documentation/tests before merge.

options.title: Keep the optimization non-public
options.body: Rescope the two bundled mirrors to a private owner/runtime seam and avoid adding a public Plugin SDK runner until another supported plugin use case exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow SDK contract
recommendation.body: Approve the indexed lock as a reusable plugin API, then require current-head real behavior proof and focused compatibility documentation/tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged transcript-index foundation and the proposed follow-up API, making them the strongest technical routing contact for clarifying the intended boundary.
